nodes.content: Develop a stochastic subgrid closure that preserves energy budgets and transfers extreme-precipitation statistics across warming climates.
requirements: Under held-out 4 K warming, reduce absolute 99th-percentile precipitation bias 20% versus a deterministic closure.
Keep global energy-budget residual below 0.5 W/m² without climate-specific retuning.

nodes.content: Use a CAPE–humidity-conditioned, heavy-tailed stochastic convection closure, projecting sampled tendencies onto column energy and water budgets.
How can sampled convective extremes reflect CAPE and humidity while satisfying column energy and water conservation?
CAPE–humidity-conditioned Pareto draws with projection will reduce 4 K P99 bias ≥20% versus deterministic, maintaining global energy residual <0.5 W/m².
Fit Pareto parameters on 0/2 K data; project tendencies; compare held-out 4 K P99 against deterministic and audit energy residual.
Run ten-member held-out 4 K ensembles with frozen parameters; compare projected Pareto and deterministic P99 bias and global energy-budget residual.
Held-out 4 K: projected P99 absolute bias was 7.8 versus deterministic 10.5 mm/day (26% reduction); energy residual 0.31 W/m².
Ablate CAPE–humidity conditioning and budget projection separately in frozen-parameter 4 K ensembles; assess P99 bias and energy residual.
Ablation controls exposed wet-year vulnerability: full closure’s global energy residual reached 0.62 W/m², despite its 0.31 W/m² ensemble mean.
Globally coupled projection of CAPE–humidity Pareto heating and cloud-radiative tendencies should maintain ≥20% P99 gains and wet-year residuals <0.5 W/m².
Implement global heating–radiation projection calibrated at 0/2 K; rerun frozen-parameter 4 K ensembles, checking wet-year residuals and P99 bias.
Run ten-member frozen-parameter 4 K ensembles with globally coupled heating–radiation projection; score wet-year peak residual and absolute P99 bias.
Globally coupled 4 K ensembles: absolute P99 bias was 8.0 versus deterministic 10.5 mm/day; peak wet-year residual was 0.38 W/m².
Adopt globally coupled projection: it retains P99 gains while resolving the original closure’s wet-year energy-budget breach without climate-specific retuning.
Train a Clausius–Clapeyron-normalized conditional flow for joint precipitation–radiation anomalies, enforcing energy and water conservation through flux-form sampling.
Can Clausius–Clapeyron normalization stabilize the conditional flow’s 4 K precipitation tail while flux-form sampling preserves energy and water budgets?
Frozen 0/2 K Clausius–Clapeyron-normalized flux-form flow will cut 4 K P99 bias ≥20% versus deterministic; energy residual <0.5 W/m².
Train the normalized flux-form flow at 0/2 K; freeze weights, then evaluate ten-member 4 K P99 bias and energy residual.
Run ten-member held-out 4 K ensembles using frozen normalized flux-form flow; compare P99 bias against deterministic and audit energy residual.
Held-out 4 K: flow P99 bias 7.2 versus deterministic 10.5 mm/day (31% lower); global energy-budget residual 0.42 W/m².
4K-FlowEval-v1 bundle contains ten-member P99 scores, deterministic baseline comparisons, global energy-budget audits, and reproducible run seeds.
Use Markov-switching entraining plumes with saturation-humidity-scaled moisture supply and explicit column energy–water flux constraints.
Do Markov-switching plume regimes reproduce warming-sensitive P99 rainfall without violating column energy–water flux constraints?
Fit switching plumes at 0/2 K; test frozen 4 K P99 bias versus deterministic, global energy and column water residuals.
Frozen 4 K switching plumes yielded P99 bias 9.4 versus deterministic 10.5 mm/day; global energy residual reached 0.57 W/m².
Humidity-scaled transitions and global radiative projection should yield 4 K P99 bias ≤8.4 mm/day and energy residual <0.5 W/m².
Fit humidity-scaled transitions at 0/2 K, apply global radiative projection, then evaluate frozen 4 K P99 bias and energy residual.
Run frozen 4 K humidity-scaled switching plumes with global radiative projection; measure P99 bias and global energy residual.
Revised switching plumes achieved 4 K P99 bias 8.2 versus deterministic 10.5 mm/day; global energy residual 0.44 W/m².
Retain humidity-scaled, radiatively projected plumes as an interpretable benchmark: revised runs meet both thresholds; original plumes failed both.
Sample humidity-conditioned Student-t-copula rain subcolumns, conservatively exchange enthalpy and water, and constrain radiative fluxes.
Can humidity-conditioned Student-t-copula subcolumns transfer 4 K P99 rainfall while conservative exchanges keep energy residual below 0.5 W/m²?
Frozen 0/2 K Student-t-copula subcolumns will achieve 4 K P99 bias ≤8.4 mm/day and global energy residual <0.5 W/m².
Fit humidity-conditioned copula on 0/2 K data; freeze parameters, then evaluate 4 K P99 bias, energy residual and radiative-flux closure.
Using 4K-FlowEval-v1 seeds and scoring, run frozen copula 4 K ensembles; measure P99 bias, energy residual, and radiative closure.
Frozen copula at 4 K: P99 bias 8.1 versus deterministic 10.5 mm/day; global energy residual 0.46 W/m².
Copula-4K-v1 report records seed-matched P99 scores, subcolumn enthalpy–water exchanges, and global radiative-flux closure diagnostics.
Audit Copula-4K-v1 flux logs; rerun wet-year 4 K seeds to check P99 bias and energy residual against reported values.
Wet-year 4 K reruns showed P99 bias 8.3 mm/day and peak global energy residual 0.48 W/m²; subcolumn exchanges balanced.
Retain copula subcolumns as a viable benchmark: seed-matched 4 K and wet-year audits meet P99 and energy thresholds.
Sample saturation-scaled gamma autoconversion rates and ice fall speeds, conserving column water and enthalpy with global radiative projection.
Can saturation-scaled stochastic autoconversion and ice settling capture 4 K P99 rainfall without destabilizing energy and water budgets?
Frozen 0/2 K gamma microphysics will yield 4 K P99 bias ≤8.4 mm/day and global energy residual <0.5 W/m².
Calibrate gamma microphysics at 0/2 K; freeze parameters, then audit held-out 4 K P99 bias and energy–water budgets.
Using Copula-4K-v1 scores and flux diagnostics, run frozen gamma-microphysics 4 K ensembles; benchmark P99 bias and energy–water closure.
Frozen gamma microphysics at 4 K: P99 bias 8.0 versus deterministic 10.5 mm/day; energy residual 0.39 W/m².
Retain gamma microphysics as a viable candidate: held-out 4 K P99 and global energy residual both meet thresholds.
